bestBets.overview: Track rated heavy 10 at the time of acceptances with a forecast for mostly sunny weather leading up to the meeting. FORMENTER raced on the pace at Strathalbyn on debut before fading late to finish fourth. He'll be better for the race experience and has favourably in barrier 3. PRETTY MORSEL worked home well from back in the field to finish third in a leader dominated race at Strathalbyn last start. The step up to 1430m looks ideal. RESILIENT RUBY has performed fairly in two runs to date. She'll find this easier and should not be overlooked. ROAD TO THE CITY led them up at Port Augusta on Sunday before tiring late.

raceTips.comment: Formenter ran well when sent out fav on debut running hen 4th behind Winning All Rund at Strathalbyn. He draws a nice gate and should take some beating. Pretty Morsel has been placed at five of 12 and was 3rd behind My Cherie Amor at Murray Bridge last time. Road To The City was OK running 3rd at Port Augusta last time and draws the inside. Resilient Ruby could be an improver.

bestBets.overview: CUTE GIRL was runner-up in a Bendigo maiden two starts ago, then went to Warracknabeal where she won with a bit in hand. WINNING ALL ROUND returned from a spell with a strong win over Blazing Red at Strathalbyn. He's bound to have taken benefit from that and has drawn favourably here in gate 3. MRS HARRIS (formerly trained by Tony & Calvin McEvoy) kicked off her last campaign with a win in a Stawell maiden. SO GRAND failed to threaten at Strathalbyn at his latest outing but two runs prior to that were full of merit. There were some excuses for ON THE MAP at her most recent run.

raceTips.comment: Winning All Round was impressive first-up from a break when a 2 length Strathalbyn winner. He’s got upside and is the horse to beat from a good barrier. Cute Girl comes off a Warracknabeal maiden win when an odds-on fav and looks the danger from a middle gate. Rhinestone Rory was a Bordertown winner three runs back and was well beaten at Mount Gambier last time. So Grand was good running 2nd at Mount Gambier two runs back. Mrs Harris won a Stawell maiden back in Jan and debut for David Page.
